questions.explanation: Workbook Q6: Locke's classical liberalism holds that individuals surrender executive power to government solely to protect their natural rights to Life, Liberty, and Property.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: What term refers to the autonomous entities and groups that operate independently of the state to express views, engage in collective action, and hold the state accountable?

options.A: Privy Council
options.B: Civil Society
options.C: Electoral College
options.D: Feudal Aristocracy

questions.explanation: Workbook Q7: Civil Society encompasses NGOs, community associations, professional bodies, and unions operating outside direct state control.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: According to liberal constitutional theory, the system of checks and balances ensures that power is divided among which three arms of government?

options.A: Monarchy, Nobility, and Clergy
options.B: Federal, State, and Local Councils
options.C: Police, Military, and Secret Service
options.D: Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary

questions.explanation: Workbook Q8: Separation of powers divides governmental authority across the Legislature (law-making), Executive (law enforcement), and Judiciary (law interpretation).

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: Which philosophical perspective views the state as an executive committee and tool of the ruling class to suppress the working class and prevent class consciousness?

options.A: Marxism
options.B: Liberalism
options.C: Fascism
options.D: Libertarianism

questions.explanation: Workbook Q9: Marxism views the state as a coercive instrument used by the bourgeoisie to maintain capitalist property relations against the proletariat.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: In which German city was the African continent arbitrarily partitioned among European colonial powers between 1884 and 1885?

options.A: Berlin
options.B: Munich
options.C: Frankfurt
options.D: Hamburg

questions.explanation: Workbook Q10: The Berlin West Africa Conference (1884–1885) hosted by Otto von Bismarck divided Africa into arbitrary colonial spheres of influence without African consent.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: What is the term for the inevitable class struggle predicted by Marx that will lead to the overthrow of the ruling class by the working class to establish an egalitarian society?

options.A: Proletarian / Socialist Revolution
options.B: Bourgeois Counter-Reformation
options.C: Mercantile Transition
options.D: Industrial Strike Wave

questions.explanation: Workbook Q11: In Marxist theory, the Proletarian Revolution overthrows capitalist domination to establish the dictatorship of the proletariat en route to a classless society.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: What term describes the exclusive authority and autonomy of a state to govern its territory without external interference, and by which 1648 treaty was it established in international law?

options.A: Sovereignty; Treaty of Westphalia (1648)
options.B: Hegemony; Treaty of Versailles (1919)
options.C: Suzerainty; Treaty of Utrecht (1713)
options.D: Imperialism; Treaty of Paris (1783)

questions.explanation: Workbook Q12: Sovereignty was established in international law by the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, cementing non-interference in domestic affairs.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: Sovereignty is understood across which two constitutional and international dimensions?

options.A: Internal and External Sovereignty
options.B: Civil and Military Sovereignty
options.C: Federal and Unitary Sovereignty
options.D: Direct and Representative Sovereignty

questions.explanation: Workbook Q13: Internal sovereignty (supreme legal authority inside territory) and External sovereignty (independence from external interference and global diplomatic recognition).

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: According to Loshkariov (2024), which combination of factors constrains empirical state sovereignty across contemporary African countries?

options.A: Imperial conquest, hereditary dynasty, and tributary vassalage
options.B: Federalism, bicameral legislature, and judicial precedent
options.C: Internal sovereignty, external sovereignty, and international diplomatic recognition
options.D: Compulsory military conscription, standing naval fleet, and state religion

questions.explanation: Workbook Q14: Loshkariov (2024) identifies weak state institutions, heavy foreign debt burdens, porous borders, and external geopolitical manipulation as key sovereign constraints.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: In Nigeria's Middle Belt region, violent farmer-herder clashes are primarily exacerbated by what factors?

options.A: Sectarian theological doctrinal disputes over ecclesiastical authority
options.B: Contested constitutional jurisdiction over municipal municipal tax collection
options.C: Conflicting corporate maritime concessions across transboundary exclusive economic zones
options.D: Ecological pressures, desertification, and competition over arable land and grazing routes

questions.explanation: Workbook Q15: Drought and desertification drive pastoralists southward, colliding with sedentary agrarian communities over arable grazing lands and water points.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: What was the precise duration of the Nigerian Civil War?

options.C: July 1967 to January 1970

questions.explanation: Workbook Q16: The Nigerian Civil War raged from 6 July 1967 until 15 January 1970 with General Yakubu Gowon declaring 'No Victor, No Vanquished'.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: What was the crowning achievement of the post-apartheid Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) in South Africa?

options.A: Summary military executions of high-ranking apartheid military commanders
options.B: Restorative justice, public truth-telling, and conditional amnesty for human rights violations
options.C: Expropriation of all industrial corporate assets without compensation
options.D: Strict statutory disenfranchisement of former minority party voters

questions.explanation: Workbook Q17: The TRC, chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, prioritized restorative justice, truth-telling, and amnesty over bloody vengeance.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: Karl Marx identified which two antagonistic social classes in capitalist society as continually locked in conflict?

options.A: Feudal Lords and Serfs
options.B: Guild Masters and Apprentices
options.C: Clergy and Laity
options.D: The Bourgeoisie (capitalists) and the Proletariat (working class)

questions.explanation: Workbook Q18: In Marxist sociology, the Bourgeoisie own the means of production while the Proletariat own only their labour power which they sell for wages.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: In sociological conflict theory, what is 'Class Consciousness'?

options.A: The passive adoption of state nationalist mythology by impoverished rural peasantry
options.B: The collective self-awareness of the working class regarding their common exploitation and historic mission
options.C: The individual pursuit of upward economic mobility through competitive private enterprise
options.D: The psychological identification of workers with the ethnic heritage of factory owners

questions.explanation: Workbook Q19: Class consciousness is the transition from a 'class-in-itself' to a 'class-for-itself', uniting workers to fight for structural transformation.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: According to Karl Marx, what is the grave structural defect of a laissez-faire, unregulated free market economy?

options.A: Excessive leisure time for factory labourers
options.B: Rapid deflation making food completely free
options.C: Alienation of labour, concentration of wealth, and ruthless exploitation of the working class
options.D: Surplus tax revenue causing government stagnation

questions.explanation: Workbook Q20: Marx demonstrated that laissez-faire capitalism inevitably produces worker alienation and widens the inequality gulf between rich owners and poor workers.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: To act as a primary mediator and arbiter in conflict resolution, what three institutional mechanisms does the state deploy?

options.A: Religious rituals, secret societies, and royal decrees
options.B: Foreign mercenaries, martial law decrees, and trade embargoes
options.C: Corporate mergers, price fixing, and bank bailouts
options.D: Judicial adjudication (courts), administrative mediation/inquiry, and law enforcement / coercive peacekeeping

questions.explanation: Workbook Q21: The state deploys legal courts (adjudication), administrative commissions of inquiry (mediation), and policing agencies (peace enforcement).

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: Former UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan famously declared that which three interdependent pillars form the building blocks of human and national security?

options.A: Land, Labour, and Capital
options.B: Peace, Development, and Human Rights
options.C: Nuclear weapons, Trade surpluses, and Space satellites
options.D: Oil, Gas, and Solid minerals

questions.explanation: Workbook Q22: Kofi Annan asserted that humanity cannot enjoy development without security, nor security without development, and neither without respect for human rights.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: What are the four core characteristics of Human Security established in the landmark 1994 UNDP Human Development Report?

options.A: Universal, People-centred, Interdependent, and Early prevention
options.B: Territorial, Militaristic, Bureaucratic, and Centralized
options.C: Bilateral, Retaliatory, Covert, and Offensive
options.D: Commercial, Industrial, Financial, and Monetary

questions.explanation: Workbook Q23: The 1994 UNDP report defined Human Security as: (1) Universal, (2) People-centred, (3) Interdependent, and (4) Early prevention focused.

questions.chapter_title: The State, Conflict Resolution, and Development in Africa
questions.question: Why did the post-civil war 'No Victor, No Vanquished' declaration and '3Rs' policy (Reconstruction, Rehabilitation, Reconciliation) fall short of durable peace in Nigeria?

options.A: To enforce heavy economic reparations and territorial dismemberment on the defeated region
options.B: To dissolve all regional state borders and institute permanent military governorates
options.C: To foster national reconciliation, prevent revanchism, and facilitate reintegration under the 3Rs framework
options.D: To transfer mineral revenue management to multinational oil consortia

questions.explanation: Workbook Q24: Failure to genuinely implement the 3Rs, perceived marginalization, and weak institutional accountability prevented deep structural reconciliation.
